thread:
Samir Patel: Hey team — customer 'BrightDesk' on Dedicated is seeing intermittent 429s and huge latency spikes when they try to burst. Happening since yesterday evening. They say their app sends short bursts (~200 reqs/sec) for 30s then quiet. Dedicated pool is 'bd-reserved-eu-west'. Can we triage?

Jess Rivera: Oof. Are they hitting the per-account throttles or the pool throughput cap? Any x-rate-limit headers in responses?

Samir Patel: I asked them to paste headers, they sent back a sample.

Samir Patel: "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 22:11:02 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1687165860
Retry-After: 30

{\"error\":\"rate_limited\",\"detail\":\"reserved pool throughput exhausted\"}" 

Alex Chen: That Reset value looks unix-ish but low — hmm. Also note the error detail 'reserved pool throughput exhausted' — that implies the pool capacity (tokens/s) was hit, not the account-level quota. Do we have the pool metrics for bd-reserved-eu-west around 22:10-22:15 UTC?

Eli Turner: Pulling. I see a sustained spike: 21:58–22:14 window, aggregate tokens/sec jumped to 85% of the pool baseline, then a few 30s windows hit 115% when bursts overlapped. Autoscaling didn't spin up because policy is conservative for that pool (min nodes fixed, bursts require sustained >90% for 3m).

Maria Gomez: Customer claims they haven't changed config. They run a client-side retryer that does 5 immediate retries on 429s. Could that be amplifying?

Jess Rivera: Absolutely. Immediate retries + aggressive burst can create a retry feedback loop. Need to confirm client backoff. Also want to validate their token size distribution (short vs long outputs) — that affects token throughput.

Samir Patel: Repro steps requested from them — I suggested this curl to reproduce from their region:

Samir Patel: ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do \
  curl -sS -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-llm-13b\",\"input\":\"short prompt\",\"max_tokens\":32}' &\ndone; wait
```

Alex Chen: Good. Ask them to run with a single long-running connection (keep-alive) and then with 200 parallel connections — difference in latency and 429 patterns will point to queue/backpressure limits in the serving runtime.

Redwood Oncall Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4896 — "Dedicated pool throughput limit causing 429s for customer BrightDesk". Severity: P2. Pager duty: @oncall-eng.

Eli Turner: Quick note on metrics: pool throughput cap is configured at 12k tokens/s for bd-reserved-eu-west (committed). When bursts exceeded this, router started returning 429s with that reserved-pool detail. Autoscaling policy allows transient bursts via 'burst bucket' of 60k tokens once per 5 minutes, but if multiple tenants burst simultaneously it gets exhausted.

Jess Rivera: Is the 'burst bucket' per-pool or per-customer? If per-pool then noisy neighbors might be stealing their burst capacity.

Eli Turner: It's per-pool. We do not isolate bursts per account in Dedicated pools by default — tradeoff for utilization. We can enable per-account burst reservations but requires config change and quota adjustments.

Maria Gomez: Customer asked about billing — they saw a spike in tokens billed when retries happened. How do we explain that?

Alex Chen: Retries that succeed count as normal usage; retries that are immediately rate-limited may not bill, but retries that fall through after backoff do. In their case, the retry loop likely increased token consumption when each retry was accepted. Also if they increased max_tokens during retry tests, that would inflate cost.

Samir Patel: Customer also reported an auth error during one spike: intermittent 401s followed by 429s. Logs show a short-lived token refresh failure from their side (OAuth provider error). They retried auth continuously which led to a flurry of new sessions hitting the pool.

Jess Rivera: Classic cascade: auth retries -> new connections -> burst -> pool exhaustion -> 429 -> client retries -> loop. Need to give them concrete mitigations.

Alex Chen: Proposed mitigation steps to send to customer:
- Implement exponential backoff for 429s (jittered, start at 200ms, max 5s).
- Avoid immediate retry flood on auth failures; throttle token refresh attempts and fail early if auth provider is down.
- Use client-side concurrency limiter: cap parallel requests to 30-50 when on Dedicated with bd-reserved-eu-west.
- Pin model and max_tokens to predictable sizes to reduce variance.
- If consistent bursts needed, consider upgrading pool commit or request a dedicated burst reservation (we can provision per-account burst buffers).

Eli Turner: On our side we can:
- Temporarily raise burst bucket for bd-reserved-eu-west for 2 hours to let them finish onboarding tests (ops change).
- Add per-account burst reservations for BrightDesk — requires billing/contract sign-off.
- Review autoscale policy to allow faster warmup for small controlled bursts.

Samir Patel: I've asked customer to run the reproducible curl with: 1) 200 parallel short requests, 2) 1 long persistent connection, while we lift burst bucket. Waiting for results.

Redwood Oncall Bot: Action logged: ops-change-1372 — "Increase temporary burst allowance for bd-reserved-eu-west by 35% for 120m" (approved by Eli Turner).

Maria Gomez: I told the customer we can enable a short-term bump and will follow up with engineering. They're ok to test now.

Samir Patel: They ran both tests — results pasted:
Samir Patel: Parallel 200x: ~18% of requests got 429 in first 45s, median latency 950ms, p95 2.3s.
Samir Patel: Persistent conn: 3% 429s, median latency 420ms, p95 900ms.

Jess Rivera: That aligns with head-of-line/backpressure on concurrent connections. Persistent connections reduce overhead and firehose behavior. Good data.

Alex Chen: Next steps:
- Samir to send recommended client-side config and sample backoff code.
- Eli to monitor pool metrics and consider autoscale policy change.
- Maria to coordinate billing/contract for burst reservation if customer requests.
- Jess to add a KB article about Dedicated pool burst best practices and common pitfalls (retry loops, auth storms).

Samir Patel: I'll draft email with the reproduce curl, suggested client changes, and attach the logs.

Eli Turner: Also to note for the long term: we should evaluate per-account burst accounting for Dedicated pools and add `X-Pool-Burst-Remaining` header for better client-side visibility. I'll open an RFC.

Redwood Oncall Bot: Incident INC-2026-4896 status updated: mitigation in progress.

Maria Gomez: Customer responded: "Thanks — after you raised the burst allowance and we switched to keep-alive + reduced client concurrency the tests passed. We'll plan to request a formal burst reservation while we scale usage." :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: Closing loop — will update thread when RFC and KB are live. Thanks all for quick response.

Jess Rivera: Nice work. Add note: prod-runbook updated with 'check pool burst bucket' step.

Eli Turner: RFC created: rfc-2026-82 "Per-account burst reservations + pool-burst headers" — assigning to Alex for design review.

Samir Patel: Thread closed from support side, keeping incident open for follow-through.
